title: Writing a Quadratic Function Through Three Points
seo_title: Algebra II Quadratic Through Three Points Worksheets (TEKS 2A.4A, 2A.4E)
domain: Quadratic and Square Root Functions, Equations, and Inequalities
standard_text: 2A.4A write the quadratic function given three specified points in the plane; 2A.4E formulate quadratic and square root equations using technology given a table of data
meta_desc: Free Algebra II worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.4A and 2A.4E: write y = ax² + bx + c through three points, quadratic models from tables and projectile data. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Put each point into y = ax² + bx + c and solve for a, b and c.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Three points (with different x-values) decide exactly one parabola y = ax2 + bx + c.
  • Put each point into the equation: you get three equations in a, b and c.
  • A point (0, c) gives c right away.
  • In a table with equal steps in x, the second differences are equal to 2a.

Examples

Example

Through (0, 3), (1, 4), (2, 9)

c = 3

a + b = 1 and 4a + 2b = 6

a = 2, b = −1

Answer: y = 2x2 − x + 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using x instead of x2 with a(−2, 5) gives 4a − 2b + c = 5.
Dropping the sign of xx = −2 gives −2b.
Using the second difference as aThe second difference is 2a.

items.q: A parabola y = ax2 + bx + c passes through (−3, −8), (−1, −4), (3, −44). Which system gives a, b and c?
items.e: Put each point into y = ax2 + bx + c: x2 goes with a and x (with its sign) goes with b. 9a − 3b + c = −8; a − b + c = −4; 9a + 3b + c = −44.
